data.title: What Does a Harness Buy? Tokens, Mostly
data.description: arXiv:2610.04433v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A coding agent is a language model inside a harness: the system prompt, the tools, and the context management that let a chat model work in a repository. Most of the engineering on these agents goes into the harness, and vendors and leaderboards credit it with score gains. Earlier studies have fixed the model and swapped the harness, but have not measured whether the swap changes the pass rate more than running the same harness again. We run seven models through three production harnesses, Claude Code, mini-SWE-agent, and OpenCode, on SWE-bench Verified and two benchmarks of other kinds, and rerun them unchanged. No harness leads consistently across models. Where the data can bound the difference between two harnesses, the bound is 2 to 5 points, and a harness swap changes about as many task outcomes as a rerun. The exceptions are harness effects in particular pairings of model and harness, whose direction changes with the model: OpenCode trails by 8 to 9 points on one model and leads by 14 on another. Cost differences between harnesses also depend on the model, from under 10% to 3 to 4 times. Which harness is better therefore has no answer apart from the model, and a harness difference should be reported next to a rerun.
data.author: Yangze Liu, Zhongyi Han
